title: Violin Concerto in D major
hook: Written for a great violinist friend, with a stormy entrance, an oboe’s song and a Hungarian dance to finish.

painting.title: Picnic in May
painting.pairingNote: A sunlit picnic on a Hungarian hillside, painted a few years before the concerto, with the same open-air warmth and the Hungarian accent of its finale.

facts: Brahms wrote the concerto in the summer of 1878 at Pörtschach, on a lake in southern Austria, for his friend Joseph Joachim, the leading violinist of the day. Joachim advised on the solo part and gave the premiere in Leipzig on 1 January 1879, with Brahms conducting.
It was planned in four movements. Brahms dropped the two middle ones and replaced them with what he called a “feeble Adagio”.

The orchestra is a full partner, not a background. A joke that the piece was written “against the violin” is attributed both to the conductor Hans von Bülow and to the violinist Joseph Hellmesberger. The virtuoso Pablo de Sarasate, the story goes, refused to play it because the oboe has the only tune in the Adagio.
Brahms wrote no [[cadenza|cadenza]] for the first movement. Almost every violinist plays Joachim’s. The finale’s dance has a Hungarian flavour, a nod to Joachim, who was Hungarian.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a broad, pastoral drama with a stormy entrance (I), an oboe’s song (II), a Hungarian dance (III).

movements.heading: Allegro non troppo
movements.summary: A long movement in [[sonata-form|sonata form]] with a [[double-exposition|double exposition]]: the orchestra presents the main tunes for more than two minutes before the violin plays a note. The mood is broad and pastoral, but the violin arrives like a storm.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a calm tune that climbs up and down the notes of a D major chord, first in low strings, bassoons and horns.

mainIdeas.name: The closing theme
mainIdeas.description: a fierce, marching tune in the minor, with a dotted long-short rhythm.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 3
mainIdeas.description: a tender melody that only the violin plays, kept back for its own exposition.

stops.hear: Low strings, bassoons and horns play a calm tune; the oboe answers
stops.happening: Theme 1, from the orchestra alone

stops.hear: Everyone in a hard, loud unison; then trumpets and drums blaze out the opening tune
stops.happening: The first [[tutti|tutti]]

stops.hear: The strings break into a fierce, marching tune in the minor
stops.happening: The closing theme. It leads straight to the soloist

stops.hear: Over a drum roll, the violin bursts in alone, in the minor, racing across all four strings
stops.happening: The soloist’s entrance: a passage like a cadenza, at the start instead of the end

stops.hear: The violin, high and quiet, sings the opening tune over a light accompaniment
stops.happening: Theme 1 in the solo exposition. The storm has become calm

stops.hear: A new, tender melody from the violin, rising out of the orchestra
stops.happening: Theme 3. The orchestra never had this tune

stops.hear: The violin stops; the orchestra plays loud chords with the timpani
stops.happening: The end of the solo exposition. The [[development|development]] starts with the orchestra

stops.hear: Quieter; woodwinds pass a falling phrase from one to the next while the violin answers
stops.happening: The development, in C minor, marked *tranquillo*

stops.hear: The full orchestra with trumpets, triumphant, plays the opening tune
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

stops.hear: The violin alone, in chords, runs and long [[trill|trill]]s
stops.happening: The cadenza by Joseph Joachim

stops.hear: Strings, horns and bassoons enter softly while the violin, very high, sings the opening tune
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]. The most peaceful moment of the movement

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: Livelier; horn calls and a march in the strings, then short, sharp chords
stops.happening: A brief, quicker close, marked *animato*

notice: Compare the opening tune at ≈ 0:00 and ≈ 20:01. The same notes, first in the low instruments, then floating high on the violin after the cadenza.
At ≈ 2:35 the soloist enters in the minor and stays stormy for almost two minutes before it plays the main tune.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Mutter was eighteen when she made it with Karajan, who had championed her since her teens. The cadenza is Joachim’s.

movements.heading: Adagio
movements.summary: A slow song in three parts. The oboe has the melody first, over the wind section alone, and the violin only joins after more than two minutes. The middle part turns passionate and minor.

mainIdeas.name: The main melody
mainIdeas.description: long, calm and singing, first on the oboe over bassoons, horns and the other winds.

mainIdeas.name: The middle section
mainIdeas.description: a restless, richly decorated violin line in F-sharp minor.

stops.hear: Bassoons and horns, then the oboe begins a long, slow melody; only wind instruments play
stops.happening: The main theme. No strings yet, and no violin

stops.hear: The violin enters, soaring above the melody and decorating it
stops.happening: The soloist takes over the oboe’s tune

stops.hear: The winds slip suddenly into a far-off key; the violin grows restless
stops.happening: The turn to the middle section

stops.hear: A passionate violin line in the minor, ever more decorated
stops.happening: The middle section, in F-sharp minor

stops.hear: The oboe sings the main melody again while the violin weaves around it
stops.happening: The return of the first part

stops.hear: The violin takes the lead with a new, intense phrase
stops.happening: The emotional peak of the movement

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The violin holds the melody to a quiet close over soft wind chords
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]

notice: Listen to the opening two minutes as a piece for wind band. Brahms keeps the strings silent until the violin is about to enter.

movements.heading: Allegro giocoso, ma non troppo vivace – Poco più presto
movements.tempo: Allegro giocoso, ma non troppo vivace – Poco più presto
movements.summary: A fast [[rondo|rondo]] with a Hungarian flavour. The violin opens with a bold dance tune played on two strings at once, and the movement ends with the tune turned into a swinging march.

mainIdeas.name: The rondo theme
mainIdeas.description: a stamping, Hungarian-style dance, played by the violin in [[double-stop|double stop]]s.

mainIdeas.name: First episode
mainIdeas.description: rising scales in a dotted rhythm, answered by falling scales in the low strings.

mainIdeas.name: Second episode
mainIdeas.description: a gentle, pastoral dance in three beats.

stops.hear: The violin, playing two strings at once, a bold dance tune with a strong accent
stops.happening: The rondo theme

stops.hear: The full orchestra plays the tune, louder than before
stops.happening: The theme in the [[tutti|tutti]]

stops.hear: The violin climbs in proud, dotted scales; the low strings answer by coming down
stops.happening: The first episode, in A major

stops.hear: The dance tune slides back in
stops.happening: The rondo theme returns

stops.hear: The pulse changes to three beats: a gentle, swaying tune
stops.happening: The second episode

stops.hear: The climbing scales again, without the dance tune first
stops.happening: A surprise: the first episode returns early

stops.hear: The whole orchestra, triumphant, with the dance tune
stops.happening: The rondo theme returns at last

stops.hear: A pause; then the violin alone, in rich chords
stops.happening: A short passage like a cadenza

stops.hear: Faster; the tune becomes a swinging march over a rocking rhythm
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]], *Poco più presto*

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: Fragments of the tune between drum taps; everything grows quiet, then three loud chords
stops.happening: The end

notice: Count the times the dance tune comes back. The longest wait is between ≈ 2:11 and ≈ 5:10, which is why its return sounds so triumphant.

threads.title: A friend’s concerto
threads.body: Joachim shaped the solo part, played the premiere and wrote the cadenza; the finale’s Hungarian dance is a tribute to him.

threads.title: The orchestra as partner
threads.body: The orchestra plays the first two minutes of the first movement and the oboe opens the Adagio. The violin is often accompanist as much as soloist.

threads.title: Calm and storm
threads.body: Each movement sets a calm, singing idea against a fierce one: the pastoral opening and the stormy entrance, the oboe’s song and the minor middle section, the dance and its rhapsodic interruption.
